problem: Domain randomization and system identification are limited by simulator fidelity. Prior neural reconstruction (3DGS/NeRF) focuses on novel-view synthesis and gives no physical interaction, while mesh-based Video2Game has poor visual fidelity, so there is no scalable way to turn casual videos into realistic, interactive simulators for RL navigation.
motivation: Urban navigation robots (delivery bots, wheelchairs) are hard and risky to train in the real world, and traditional simulators have a large visual sim2real gap. Web videos are abundant, so reconstructing them into photorealistic, collidable digital twins could give scalable, low-gap RL training environments.
key_idea: Reconstruct monocular videos with geometry-consistent Gaussian Splatting and pair it with an invisible collision mesh in Unity (hybrid GS+mesh representation) with inserted static/dynamic obstacles, so RL agents train on photorealistic RGB and transfer zero-shot to the real world.
insight: Photorealistic GS observations are what close the sim2real gap: agents trained on mesh-rendered RGB (Video2Game-style) get 0% in the real world, while Vid2Sim agents reach 55-85%. Interactive obstacles matter (No Obj 68.8% -> Static 80.8% -> Dynamic 81.6% SR PointNav), and real-world success grows with the number of training scenes (1/5/30 envs: 0/60/85% Go Straight), showing scene diversity/scaling drives generalization.
method: Scale-invariant geometry supervision: patch-based NCC loss between rendered depth and Depth-Anything-V2 predicted depth, plus cosine normal loss against pseudo-GT normals from PCA on predicted-depth point clouds, avoiding SfM scale ambiguity.

Geometry-consistent loss and 2D-disk regularization: depth-gradient-weighted normal smoothness between adjacent pixels (L_geo), plus a shortest-axis scale penalty inspired by 2DGS; total loss = rgb+depth+normal+geo+scale, with AbsGS densification, DEVA dynamic masks, and GLOMAP poses.
Screen-space covariance culling: at render time, remove splats whose projected 2D covariance max-norm exceeds alpha*image area, removing floaters at off-training viewpoints (FID 214.47 -> 191.54).

Hybrid scene representation: mesh extracted via TSDF fusion of rendered depth (ground removed via normal-prior ground mask + SAM-HQ), imported into Unity as invisible collision geometry, while a custom shader renders GS for RGB/depth observations.

Interactive scene composition: randomly placed static assets (cones, bins, poles) and A*-driven pedestrians composed with GS via z-buffer occlusion for RGB and depth; safety-critical scenarios like falling trash cans/roadblocks.
Scene augmentation: Instruct 4D-to-4D video-consistent editing for lighting/season/semantics, and Unity particle systems for rain/fog/snow.

RL training: SAC on stacked 6 RGB frames (128x72) plus goal distance/heading, 2D continuous action (steer, speed), bicycle dynamics, reward with terminal, distance, steering smoothness, crash and time terms; 30 parallel envs, ~15h on one A5000.

setting.backbone: SAC RL policy trained from scratch on stacked RGB frames (reconstruction uses 3DGS with Depth Anything V2 priors)
setting.training_data: 30 real2sim GS scenes reconstructed from 9 web walking videos (15 s, 30 fps clips), 1.5M SAC steps; tested on 5 held-out scenes
setting.observation: monocular front RGB (128x72, stack of current + 5 past frames) + goal distance/heading from odometry
setting.action_space: continuous 2D control (steering/wheel rotation and speed) normalized in [-1,1]
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle variant with GT depth sensor reported only as comparison in simulation)

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark; results are on the paper's own Vid2Sim simulation benchmark and real-world tests. Reconstruction results (Table 1): PSNR 32.41, SSIM 0.927, LPIPS 0.127.
results: Vid2Sim agents reach 81.6% SR (PointNav) and 74.4% SR (SocialNav) on held-out scenes, a 32.8% and 31.2% improvement over a mesh-observation baseline (48.8% / 43.2%). In real-world zero-shot deployment the mesh baseline gets 0% on all tasks, while Vid2Sim (30 envs) gets 85/65/55%. Reconstruction beats 3DGS, 2DGS, Instant-NGP and Video2Game in PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS.
limitations: Building each environment is slow (GLOMAP for poses/init), so only 30 scenes were collected; scaling is limited.
Small real-world evaluation (20 trials per task) with a single wheeled robot, and dynamic-obstacle success is only 55%.
Compares only against a self-built mesh-observation baseline since no prior video-to-sim RL pipeline exists; other embodiments (legged, humanoid) untested.
